deviation: The draft largely meets the standard (skill and care, qualified personnel, SOW-based services) and adds Arcadia-favourable terms (reports, subcontractor consent). However, 3.2 makes the Agreement body prevail over a SOW unless the SOW expressly identifies the overriding provision. That is a mild departure from the standard, and it could stop Arcadia's bespoke SOW terms from applying. Section 3.5 adds an Arcadia dependency obligation with no relief mechanism spelled out, so Helix may use it to excuse delays.
suggested_text: 3.1 Performance. Helix shall perform the Services described in each Statement of Work signed under this Agreement with reasonable skill and care, using suitably qualified personnel, and in accordance with generally accepted industry standards. 3.2 Statements of Work. Services are procured only through Statements of Work or Work Orders signed by both Parties. Each SOW forms part of this Agreement. In the event of conflict, the body of this Agreement prevails over a SOW unless the SOW expressly identifies the provision of this Agreement it intends to override and is signed by an authorised representative of Arcadia. 3.5 Arcadia Responsibilities. Arcadia shall provide timely access to information, systems and personnel reasonably required by Helix to perform the Services. Helix shall notify Arcadia in writing promptly, and in any event within five (5) business days, of any failure by Arcadia to do so. Helix shall be relieved from liability for a resulting delay only to the extent it has given that notice. [3.3, 3.4 and 3.6 as drafted.]
